start.text: Steps are cut into the stack's flank, worn hollow. At the top, a low door of tarred planks under a lintel of black stone, an iron anchor let into it: Wrackholm's sign. It isn't locked. Nothing out here ever needed locking.
Inside, a stair turns up round the wall in the dark, every tread wet. You climb it by the ember.

room.text: The lantern room is framed in ships' timbers: eight of them, tarred black, curved still with the shape of the hulls they came out of. And on every one, the yard's lead tag, nailed on, the way the salvage on the hard is tagged.
Scratched in the lead: KITTIWAKE. HONEST WEIGHT. TWO SISTERS. FAIR RETURN. The names are older than the timbers look. The fog hasn't touched these; nobody here had ever forgotten them.
A year and a tide, the yard holds what the sea gives back, for its owner to come for. And if nobody comes, it seems, it goes out to the Wrack, and holds up the light.
Between two of the timbers there's a new iron bracket, bright where it's been fitted, with nothing in it yet.

The cradle in the middle of the room is cold, salt-white with spray. Your ember leans toward it, the way it leaned at the others, and then gives up. You know the shape of this by now: it won't burn what nobody holds.

Through the dark panes, across the Teeth, a line of firelight in the lane-house shutters. The answering horn is a black stroke by the door, its bell turned this way. A horn and a light, facing each other over the water, each waiting on the other.

again.text: The Wrack's lantern room: eight tagged timbers, the new empty bracket, the cold cradle. Across the Teeth, the horn waits with its bell turned this way.
Wenna's answer is in your satchel: a brass mouthpiece gone the silver of the fog, cold as a stone.
The Gannet's crew board is in your satchel, three names chalked on black.
Hale's white-lead pot is in your satchel, grey at the lip, heavier than it looks.
It wants something somebody on Wrackholm holds. You've nothing of theirs to set in it: ask on the hard. Wenna, by the horn. The yard. Jory.

lit.text: You climb to the lantern room. The Wrack Light burns gold behind its horn panes, and the tagged timbers stand round it holding it up.
In the flame, for a heartbeat, a curl of brass. Then it's only fire.
In the flame, for a heartbeat, chalk letters on black. Then it's only fire.
In the flame, for a heartbeat, a hand of white. Then it's only fire.
Across the Teeth, the answering horn stands open by the lane-house door, its bell to the light.

waiting.text: The cradle waits. Whatever you set in it, Wrackholm will never remember again.

choice.text: Set Wenna's answer in the cradle.
Set the Gannet's crew board in the cradle.
Set Hale's white-lead pot in the cradle.

weigh_answer.text: The brass is cold in your hand, and small, for what's in it. An old woman on a coil of hawser in every weather for fifty years, answering boats home: long and two short, long and two short, and every one of them coming in on it.
And one at dusk, three months gone, that brought the Gannet onto the Teeth.
Burn it, and nobody on Wrackholm will remember Wenna Garrow ever answered a horn. Not the boats she brought home, and not the one she didn't. Not her.
Jory will never know it was her.

weigh_board.text: Three names in chalk on black: HALE CORBET, master. ANNIS CORBET. RUAN PASK. Your ember brought them back once. The Wrack won't give them back twice.
Burn it, and the Gannet's crew are nobody's again on Wrackholm, for good. Wenna will count to three and no further. Jory will have a gap where a brother was, and no name to put in it.
The new bracket will stay theirs. Nobody will know whose.

weigh_white.text: A lampwarden's pot, crusted white. In it: a boy of seven on the Teeth at the bottom of the springs, looking at nothing but the white, because he was told to; and ahead of him, carrying the pot because Hale let him, his brother.
Burn it, and Jory will never have been out on the Teeth. Nobody left on Wrackholm will have walked behind a lampwarden; come spring, whoever paints the white will be learning it off the marks.
It's the one thing Jory has of Ruan that's only his.

burn_answer.text: You lay the mouthpiece in the iron, its cord coiled round it. For a moment you'd swear you hear it: long, and two short, a long way off, coming home.

burn_board.text: You lay the board in the cradle chalk up. The names go first, letter by letter, the way they came back: HALE. ANNIS. RUAN. Then the black.

burn_white.text: You set the pot in the iron. The white at its lip catches before anything else does, and burns the colour of a spring morning.

kindle.text: The Wrack Light catches. Gold comes out through the horn panes and goes down onto the Teeth, and every timber round you is lit along its length: KITTIWAKE, HONEST WEIGHT, TWO SISTERS, FAIR RETURN, the lead tags bright as coins.

The fog leans back off the reef the way water goes off the Teeth at the ebb: a long while, and then all at once. Not gone. Standing back. Below, rock to rock to the spit, the white lies in the light, a hand on each.
Across the water the lane-house door opens and people come out onto the shingle, one and then a dozen, and stand looking. Nobody shouts. Tidewrights don't, at a lighting.
By the horn, an old woman gets up off her coil of hawser and looks at the light, and then at her own empty hand, as if she'd set something down and can't think what.
On the shingle somebody starts to say three names, the way you'd count a crew aboard, and gets to the first, and stops.
On the shingle a lanky lad in a red gansey looks out at the white lying rock to rock in the gold, as if he's never seen it before. He hasn't, now.
The answering horn is a black stroke by the lane-house door, its bell turned to you. Still lashed. A horn answered is a lane promised; it's Wenna's to promise.
The new bracket between the timbers stays empty. It's the Gannet's, whoever she was.
The new bracket between the timbers stays empty, for the Gannet. One day it'll hold her.
